items.t: Did GTA 6 really recreate Charlie Kirk's assassination?
items.m: Just days after its release, Grand Theft Auto 6 has become a vehicle for political misinformation. Viral footage falsely claims the game features a mission recreating Charlie Kirk’s assassination, while pro-Russian accounts are sharing fake screenshots containing anti-Ukrainian messages. Meanwhile, Russia’s own Defence Ministry has exploited the game's popularity to promote military recruitment. Vedika Bahl explains how GTA 6 is being used to push real political agendas in Truth or Fake.

items.m: The Kremlin’s rehabilitation of Stalin, who presided over the brutal labor camps of the Gulag, has accelerated during Russia’s war in Ukraine.

items.t: Why Russia Is Erasing Stalin’s Crimes
items.m: Across Russia, memorials to victims of Joseph Stalin’s repressive regime are being quietly dismantled as more and more critics of the war in Ukraine are jailed. Our Moscow correspondent Valerie Hopkins takes us to one example of this erasure.

items.t: Zelensky says Trump calling Putin ‘my friend’ is like being buddies with Hitler in WWII
items.m: Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky said US ⁠President Donald ⁠Trump calling Russia’s ⁠Vladimir Putin “my friend” was strange and akin to making the same comment about Adolf Hitler during World War II. In an interview ‌with the BBC, the Ukrainian president said it was up to Trump what he said or posted but he called it “strange” to call Putin a friend. “He’s an aggressor … and a killer. He can’t be ⁠a friend,” he said, speaking in English. “It’s the same that ‌somebody says about Hitler during the...

items.t: Pro-Ukraine and pro-EU presidential candidates struggle to engage French voters on these issues
items.m: Centrist candidates who advocate a tough line against Moscow have struggled to engage voters on international issues, with purchasing power and public debt at the top of people's concerns.

items.t: EU leaders fail to bridge budget splits as talks stall
items.m: Aid for Ukraine was among the disputes as EU members hope to conclude talks by the end of the year.

items.t: EU leaders split over budget spending and a $49 billion loan to Ukraine
items.m: French President Emmanuel Macron set an end-of-year deadline for an agreement on the European Union's next seven-year budget after the continent's leaders ruled out any chances for a deal to be reached at their summit on Thursday.

items.t: Live: Trump calls on Putin to end all 'military aggression' against Europe
items.m: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he had urged his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe". Although Trump did not provide any further details, he added that he hoped this would pave the way for a peace deal to be struck between Kyiv and Moscow. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

items.t: Trump unilaterally changes joint statement with NATO chief, adding warning for Ukraine not to escalate war, Politico reports
items.m: US President Donald Trump unilaterally edited the text of a joint statement with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, Politico reported.

items.t: Four Jehovah's Witnesses convicted of 'extremism' in Russian-annexed Crimea
items.m: Nov 27 - Four Jehovah's Witnesses have been convicted of \"extremist\" activity in Russian-annexed Crimea and sentenced to up to eight years in prison, the faith group said, among the longest terms handed to members since Moscow banned the movement in 2017.

items.t: Russia’s hybrid war on Europe evolving, but failing: IISS
items.m: Growing attacks have damaged European infrastructure, but have not reduced support for Ukraine, analysis says.

items.t: Tyson Fury’s wife backtracks on claim boxer suffers from schizophrenia
items.m: Paris Fury had claimed mental health diagnosis for Tyson following his 2015 victory over Ukraine's Wladimir Klitschko.

items.t: Ukraine: Residents brace for another difficult winter
items.m: As Russia continues to target Ukraine's energy infrastructure, residents are preparing for another difficult winter of strikes and power cuts. With supply chains under pressure, food prices are also rising, forcing many Ukrainians to cut back on essentials or stock up ahead of the coming months.

items.t: EU: Leaders fail to reach agreement on next budget after tense summit
items.m: At the bloc headquarters in Brussels on Thursday, EU leaders failed to reach a consensus after more than 12 hours of talks over the budget and a new $49 billion loan for Ukraine’s economic and military needs next year. France 24's Dave Keating tells us more.

items.t: ‘He’s an aggressor and a killer. He can’t be a friend’: Zelensky likens Trump calling Putin his friend to calling Hitler a friend during World War II
items.m: Volodymyr Zelensky said he finds it “strange” that Donald Trump has twice called Vladimir Putin his friend.

items.t: Crimean Court Jails 4 Jehovah’s Witnesses for ‘Extremism’
items.m: The jail terms are some of the longest handed down to members of the religious movement since it was outlawed by Russia in 2017.
